improvement_directive: Construct an observable higher-order or orthogonalized estimator whose pilot-projection remainder is uniformly no larger than the intrinsic quadratic scale n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}, thereby matching the sign-mixture converse throughout the d>=1 quadratic zone. Then prove a common-multiplier calibration using the estimated linear and quadratic components with uniform remainder control across equality, local, critical, and regular regimes.
critique: For d>=1, the central point-estimation theorem proves the intrinsic lower frontier but only a strictly slower pilot-limited observable upper bound, so it does not deliver the advertised sharp joint minimax phase diagram in the nontrivial quadratic zone. The mixed spectral-transition theorem concerns an infeasible population-score, population-kernel statistic and supplies neither an observable limit theorem nor the promised all-regime confidence procedure. The matched minimax result and exact null law for d=0 concern the separate no-covariate branch and do not close the conditional problem. The project justification incorrectly says observable calibration is the remaining open problem, because tightness of the d>=1 point-estimation bracket is also explicitly left open. What is settled therefore supports a field contribution, not a flagship resolution.
